question: What core filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose: deny-wins `allowedPaths`/`denyPaths`, access-mode roots, a narrower denyPaths escape hatch, or no host path ACL beyond workspaceOnly/container isolation?
rationale: The request defines a public config surface and an operator-facing security boundary; the current open PRs show different designs with different compatibility and false-security tradeoffs.

options.title: Settle one tools.fs contract
options.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging an implementation.

options.title: Land file tools first, split exec
options.body: Accept a file-tool-only boundary only if docs and issue state that shell-mediated file access remains a separate tracked security boundary.

options.title: Defer host path ACLs
options.body: Keep Docker, OS-user isolation, tool allow/deny, and hooks as the supported boundary if maintainers decide host path ACLs should not live in core.

recommendation.title: Settle one tools.fs contract
recommendation.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging an implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already framed the prior keep-open review and has the strongest current history around the config/schema and workspaceOnly security path.
